transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Eleanor Novak (CISO, BlueRidge), Carlos Mendes (Head of Platform), Priya Rao (Legal Ops)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private can meet BlueRidge's compliance and data residency requirements. Discussed SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO (SAML) + SCIM, RBAC and least privilege, audit logging granularity, encryption and KMS options, data retention and deletion, and initial pilot sizing. Action: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs + Dedicated pricing, customer to return specific audit log fields and schedule infra deep dive.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001)
- SSO/SAML and provisioning (SCIM)
- RBAC, separation of duties, tenant isolation
- Audit logs: retention, retention location, field-level details
- Encryption at rest + KMS/HSM integrations
- Data residency, retention, deletion and e-discovery
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Jamie Lin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jamie, AE on the account, with Samir from our security/infra team.
[00:00:12] Eleanor Novak: Hi, Eleanor here, CISO at BlueRidge. Carlos and Priya are on as well. We wanted to run through your security posture before we pull procurement.
[00:00:22] Samir Patel: Great, thanks Eleanor. Do you want to quickly share top requirements so I can call out where Redwood maps to them?
[00:00:28] Eleanor Novak: Sure. High level — SOC2 Type II or equivalent, ISO27001 preferred but not mandatory, SSO with SAML and SCIM, fine grained RBAC, encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS for any persistent customer data, audit logs with at least 12 months retention in our region, and data residency — we need EU and US separation depending on fund jurisdictions.
[00:00:48] Carlos Mendes: Also need to understand whether the Hosted API ever touches PII; we need export controls and e-discovery support.
[00:00:55] Samir Patel: Understood. To clarify from Redwood's side: for Hosted we are SOC2 Type II, we have an ISO27001 certification in-scope for the control plane (we'll share the artifacts). Hosted stores logs and telemetry in region-backed buckets and can be configured with region routing; however, Hosted data will traverse Redwood's control plane. If you need strict separation or customer-managed networking, our Dedicated or Private options provide VPC peering and air-gapped deployments.
[00:01:25] Eleanor Novak: When you say "customer-managed networking" for Private, does that mean the inference clusters never leave our VPC?
[00:01:31] Samir Patel: Correct — for Private on-prem or VPC-hosted we deploy the serving runtime inside your network. You control the network egress and KMS keys. For Dedicated we run in our infra but can isolate a GPU pool per customer with dedicated tenancy and strict tenancy controls, and we can integrate your KMS via a customer keywrap/CMK pattern.
[00:01:55] Priya Rao: What's the difference for audit logs between Hosted and Dedicated? Is the log schema the same?
[00:02:02] Samir Patel: The schema is functionally equivalent. Hosted logs are stored in our managed systems but we provide export hooks — S3-compatible exports, streaming to your SIEM, and we keep audit trails of admin actions. For Dedicated we can push logs to your cloud account directly or set up cross-account logging, which many of our enterprise customers prefer. There's also an option to increase log retention beyond default 90 days.
[00:02:28] Carlos Mendes: Can you confirm what fields are present in the audit log? We need creator, request id, model id, input hash, anonymized prompt metadata, user id, session id, response token counts, and region.
[00:02:40] Samir Patel: Yes, we capture request_id, timestamp, caller_identity, model_version, token_usage, response_status, latency_ms, and region. We do store anonymized prompt metadata — full input text is considered customer data and retention is configurable. I'll follow up with a sample log schema.
[00:02:58] Eleanor Novak: What's your stance on prompt-data retention for Hosted? We can't have customer PII persist beyond our retention window.
[00:03:06] Jamie Lin: Right — by default Hosted retains request payloads for troubleshooting and quality for a short window, and we provide configurable retention policies. For higher compliance needs we recommend Dedicated or Private, where you can set retention to zero or keep everything inside your KMS-encrypted buckets.
[00:03:22] Carlos Mendes: How does encryption/keys work for Dedicated? Can we bring our own keys (BYOK) via AWS KMS or an HSM?
[00:03:29] Samir Patel: Yes — for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS keys (CMKs). We use envelope encryption; the data-in-use on the GPU is ephemeral and not stored on disk, but persistent cache and logs are encrypted with your CMK when configured. For Private installs you have full control and can plug into your HSM.
[00:03:47] Priya Rao: Are you SOC2 + ISO reports sharable under NDA? How granular are they?
[00:03:53] Jamie Lin: We can share SOC2 Type II and our ISO scope under an NDA. Samir will attach the audit report and our SOC2 auditor letter; the ISO scope will show which services are covered.
[00:04:03] [00:04:05] Eleanor Novak: Okay, send that please. Also need evidence of penetration testing cadence and an incident response playbook.
[00:04:12] Samir Patel: We run annual pentests and quarterly internal red-team exercises; we have published incident response SLAs and will include our playbook excerpt showing escalation paths.
[00:04:22] Carlos Mendes: On SSO, we use Okta and require SAML with SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM for user provisioning?
[00:04:29] Samir Patel: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. For Dedicated we can disable Redwood-managed user stores and point to your IdP. RBAC maps to groups sent over SCIM; we also support custom roles via our console and API.
[00:04:44] Eleanor Novak: For Audit — do you provide immutable logs or just append-only with write-once policies? We need defensible audit trails for compliance audits.
[00:04:52] Samir Patel: Logs are append-only and we offer WORM-like retention options when exporting to your S3 with object lock enabled. For Hosted-managed logs we preserve integrity via checksums and retention locks; for Dedicated we recommend pushing logs into your account and enabling object-lock to meet legal hold requirements.
[00:05:10] Priya Rao: How quickly can you redact or delete data? We may need to comply with subject access requests and specific deletion requests within 30 days.
[00:05:19] Jamie Lin: Deletion requests are supported. For Hosted we can expire data and scrub prod caches on request; Dedicated/Private gives you control to run deletions in your environment. We will include the deletion procedure in the artifacts.
[00:05:35] [00:05:40] Carlos Mendes: Performance question — if we move to Dedicated, do we still get Redwood updates and runtime improvements? How are upgrades handled?
[00:05:48] Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated gets runtime improvements; upgrades are coordinated. We do canary upgrades on infra and provide rollback. For Private on-prem there is an upgrade cadence that we coordinate with your platform team; we can do air-gapped releases with signed artifacts.
[00:06:07] Eleanor Novak: Any known compliance gaps we should be aware of? For example, is there any PCI or HIPAA boundary limitations?
[00:06:14] Samir Patel: We support HIPAA covered workloads with a BAA; some customers use Private mode for strict HIPAA and PCI workloads. PCI has specific networking and cardholder data restrictions — we recommend Private for PCI scope. We'll include guidance in the security pack.
[00:06:30] [00:06:35] Jamie Lin: A couple clarifying points: BlueRidge mentioned EU/US separation — do you need Multi-region Dedicated pools or full separate Private deployments per region?
[00:06:44] Carlos Mendes: Ideally separate deployments per fund region; at minimum we need data not to leave designated regions. Routing and model selection by region is important.
[00:06:52] Samir Patel: We have region routing policy — requests can be pinned to region and we can route to nearest cluster. For strict separation we recommend Private per region or a Dedicated cluster per region with cross-account logging.
[00:07:07] [00:07:10] Priya Rao: Legal question — do you sign custom data processing addendums and can you include specific retention clauses?
[00:07:16] Jamie Lin: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can negotiate retention clauses in enterprise contracts; we'll pass to legal.
[00:07:22] Eleanor Novak: What about access controls for vendor employees and your SOC team? We need periodic access review and just-in-time admin escalation.
[00:07:30] Samir Patel: We operate least-privilege; for hosted environments access to customer data is tightly controlled and audited. We support JIT access with approval flows for support sessions and require 2-person approval for sensitive ops for customers on Dedicated.
[00:07:47] [00:07:50] Carlos Mendes: Does Redwood capture model inputs in logs for retraining? We have concerns about accidental retention for PII in prompts.
[00:07:57] Samir Patel: We separate telemetry used for model improvements from customer prompt data. By default, prompt data may be used for improvement unless you opt out. We can disable prompt retention for specific customers and opt out of training usage in enterprise contracts.
[00:08:16] Eleanor Novak: Good. We will need a contractual opt-out for training and a commitment to not use data for model improvement for the pilot.
[00:08:23] Jamie Lin: Noted — we'll include a training opt-out clause in the pilot SOW.
[00:08:28] [00:08:30] Priya Rao: On the topic of compliance evidence, can you provide a pen test report redacted for third parties?
[00:08:36] Samir Patel: Yes, we can provide a redacted pentest summary under NDA showing scope, findings, and mitigation timeline.
[00:08:44] [00:08:50] Carlos Mendes: For the pilot, we'd like to validate latency and e2e encryption. Can Redwood run a small benchmark in our region and share telemetry?
[00:08:58] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll propose a pilot architecture: a 2-week Dedicated pilot with a small GPU pool in our nearest region, cross-account logs to your S3, and KMS integration. We'll produce a benchmark sheet with latency percentiles and token costs.
[00:09:15] Eleanor Novak: Sounds good. Pricing is another consideration — we need to understand unit economics for Dedicated vs Hosted — there's a tradeoff between cost and complete control.
[00:09:23] Jamie Lin: We'll send a breakdown showing per-token and per-hour GPU costs for Hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity and an example run-rate for your expected volume.
[00:09:31] [00:09:35] Priya Rao: Anything else on consent/e-discovery? We need a documented process for legal holds and export of logs.
[00:09:41] Samir Patel: Yes, we have an e-discovery playbook and the ability to put holds on exported logs, with cross-account snapshots. We'll include a sample workflow.
[00:09:54] [00:10:00] Jamie Lin: Quick check — is it safe to say the immediate next steps are: Samir sends SOC2/ISO + pentest summary, Jamie sends pricing and pilot SOW, and customer returns audit-log field list and schedules infra deep dive?
[00:10:10] Eleanor Novak: Yes, that covers it. We'll aim to review docs by 10/15 and set the deep dive for week of 10/18.
[00:10:17] Carlos Mendes: One small nit — does Redwood provide signed artifacts for Private deployments? We need to verify binary integrity before installation.
[00:10:24] Samir Patel: Yes, for air-gapped Private installs we provide signed artifacts and checksums; we can also run a reproducible build if required.
[00:10:33] [00:10:38] Priya Rao: Great. Any potential blockers for us to get started on pilot?
[00:10:43] Jamie Lin: We need a short MSA + DPA and a pilot SOW; once those are signed we can schedule the Dedicated cluster provisioning. The SOC2/ISO artifacts should help procurement move faster.
[00:10:55] Eleanor Novak: Perfect. We'll get the legal templates over to you and aim to move quickly.
[00:11:02] [00:11:05] Jamie Lin: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and SOW.

Recap (end of call):
- Redwood to share SOC2 Type II, ISO scope doc, pentest summary, incident response playbook excerpt, and sample audit log schema (Samir).
- Redwood to send Dedicated pricing sheet and pilot SOW (Jamie).
- BlueRidge to share required audit log fields and schedule technical deep dive (Carlos/Eleanor).
- Contract/legal: discuss DPA retention clauses and training opt-out (Priya).

Keywords: SOC2, ISO27001, SAML, SCIM, RBAC, KMS, HSM, audit logs, WORM, data retention, e-discovery, pilot, Dedicated, Private, Hosted
